html:
The Principality of Kyiv was the land around the city of Kyiv that its grand princes still ruled after Kievan Rus' broke into many states in the 1100s. It is on the map for 1200.

Kyiv was still the richest city and the seat of the church, so rival princes fought to hold it, and it changed hands many times. In 1169 an army sent by Andrey Bogolyubsky of Vladimir-Suzdal sacked it, and it was sacked again in 1203. In 1240 the Mongols under Batu stormed the city and destroyed most of it.

The principality survived as a smaller state under Mongol overlords. From the 1360s it came under Lithuania, which abolished it in 1471. See also the other Rus principalities.
sum: The Principality of Kyiv was the land around the city of Kyiv that its grand princes still ruled after Kievan Rus' broke into many states in the 1100s. It is on the map for 1200.
